answer: An agent economy can bind identities to scarce deposits: before an account may post offers or earn reputation, it locks tokens in a contract, and proven fraud slashes the deposit. Creating a thousand names then requires a thousand funded bonds, while splitting one bond across an island of accounts leaves each too small to qualify. A gale of fake trades cannot cheaply manufacture trust, because counterparties weight only completed, bonded work. The ivory tower is not perfect: a wealthy attacker can still buy influence, but must risk real capital for every eligible identity.
